limitations: The unchanged player_1/player_2 motion samples still grow with frame count; sanitize(metadata) temporarily copies those movement arrays.
Selected player boxes, positions, timestamps, ball trajectories and event/analytics structures retain existing whole-clip growth; browser arrays remain outside this unit.
Sequence slices explicitly requested by a caller materialize that requested slice; production render/export use indexed reads/iteration.
Temporary database disk bytes grow with accepted observations; no full-match or independent pose/racket accuracy qualification follows from this review.
Exception tracebacks can retain the current observation/codec/decoded frame and unchanged whole-clip pipeline arrays; no new all-pose/all-racket Python list is retained by these sequences.

Snapshot semantics assume append-time observations: substitute trackers that mutate the same previously returned mapping across frames have a different alias contract from the built-in fresh-mapping producers.
mode: Independent read-only source and existing-test review; no test, inference, model, benchmark or source mutation performed
assessedInvariants: Snapshot encode immediately after each built-in observation releases original pose/racket records; built-in producers create fresh mappings rather than mutating earlier records.
Identity dictionaries retain insertion order and typed integer keys, so identity==1 render coloring and iteration remain unchanged.
Scalar IEEE bytes and safe numeric NumPy dtype/shape/buffer codec preserve exact raw values until existing sanitizer/export.
Negative indexed reads normalize before lookup; SQLite cursors close before decode/yield.

Both temporary stores are registered in the outer ExitStack before observation work and remain open through render/export. Failed second-store setup, observation, render and serialization unwind registered stores and remove exact owned files; cleanup errors are notes on the original error.
Capture/writer release contexts are registered before reads or drawing and ExitStack releases other handles if one release fails, including while traceback frames remain alive.

Raw metadata is sanitized before attaching the lazy frame adapter; dictionary key order, indentation, native text newlines, no final newline and disabled [] remain consistent with the preserved implementation.
